Here is the full MSBuild project file review for this repository.

---

# MSBuild Project File Review — ContosoApp

**Scope:** 5 project files (3 src, 2 test) · No `Directory.Build.props`, `Directory.Build.targets`, or `Directory.Packages.props` found.

---

## 🔴 Errors — Likely to Cause Runtime or Build Issues

### 1. Package version mismatch: `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions`

| Project | Version |
|---|---|
| `ContosoApp.Core` | **8.0.0** |
| `ContosoApp.Services` | **8.0.1** |
| `ContosoApp.Api` | **8.0.0** |

`ContosoApp.Api` references both `Core` (8.0.0) and `Services` (8.0.1). NuGet will unify to 8.0.1 at restore time, but this silent unification is fragile — it can produce **MSB3277** (assembly version conflict) warnings when bindings shift, and it's a correctness hazard when versions with breaking changes diverge further. All consumers should agree on a single version.

**Fix:** Centralize via Central Package Management (see recommendation below). In the interim, align all three to `8.0.1`.

### 2. Package version mismatch: test infrastructure packages

| Package | `Core.Tests` | `Api.Tests` |
|---|---|---|
| `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk` | **17.10.0** | **17.9.0** |
| `xunit` | **2.8.1** | **2.7.1** |
| `xunit.runner.visualstudio` | **2.8.1** | **2.5.6** |

These are non-trivial version gaps (full minor version differences). Mismatched test SDK versions mean:
- Different test discovery/execution behavior between test projects
- Risk of "works in one test project, fails in another" due to xunit API differences (2.7 → 2.8 changed assertion APIs)
- CI flakiness when runner versions disagree

**Fix:** Align to the latest versions across both test projects.

---

## 🟡 Warnings — Anti-Patterns to Fix

### 3. Massive property duplication across all 5 projects

Every single project file repeats these 6 properties identically:

```xml
<TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
<Nullable>enable</Nullable>
<ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
<TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
<EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>true</EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>
<Company>Contoso</Company>
<Authors>Contoso Engineering</Authors>
```

This is the textbook case for **`Directory.Build.props`**. When the TFM needs to change to `net9.0`, you'll need to edit 5 files — and miss one.

**Fix:** Create `/Directory.Build.props` at the repo root (see consolidated fix below).

### 4. Duplicated `DocumentationFile` property in all 3 src projects

All three src projects repeat:
```xml
<DocumentationFile>$(OutputPath)$(AssemblyName).xml</DocumentationFile>
```

This should also live in `Directory.Build.props`, conditionally scoped to src projects (see fix below).

### 5. Duplicated `PrintBuildInfo` custom target in all 3 src projects

All three src projects contain an identical custom target:
```xml
<Target Name="PrintBuildInfo" BeforeTargets="Build">
  <Message Importance="high" Text="Building $(AssemblyName) [$(Configuration)]" />
</Target>
```

This target also has **no `Inputs`/`Outputs`**, which means it runs on every build including no-op rebuilds. For a `Message` task this is low-impact, but it sets a bad precedent — any future custom targets following this pattern will break incremental build.

**Fix:** Move to `/Directory.Build.targets` (targets with `BeforeTargets`/`AfterTargets` belong in `.targets`, not `.props`).

### 6. No Central Package Management (CPM)

With 8 distinct packages across 5 projects (and 2 already mismatched), this repo is a prime candidate for CPM. Without it, every `dotnet add package` can introduce a new version skew.

### 7. Redundant `System.Text.Json` reference in `ContosoApp.Api`

`ContosoApp.Api` uses `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web`, which already brings in `System.Text.Json` as a framework reference on `net8.0`. The explicit `<PackageReference Include="System.Text.Json" Version="8.0.5" />` is unnecessary and can cause version conflicts if the framework ships a different version. The same package in `Core` (non-Web SDK) is fine — class libraries do need the explicit reference.

**Fix:** Remove the `System.Text.Json` PackageReference from `ContosoApp.Api.csproj`. It's already available via the shared framework.

### 8. Split `PropertyGroup` elements in src projects

`Core`, `Services`, and `Api` each have two separate `<PropertyGroup>` blocks — one for the main properties and a second for just `DocumentationFile`. There's no condition differentiating them, so they should be merged for clarity.

**Fix:** Moot once `DocumentationFile` moves to `Directory.Build.props`.

---

## 🔵 Suggestions — Improvements for Maintainability

### 9. Test projects should set `<IsTestProject>true</IsTestProject>` explicitly

While the `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk` package sets this implicitly, being explicit makes it easier to write conditions in `Directory.Build.props` (e.g., to exclude test projects from documentation generation). Both test projects already set `IsPackable=false`, which is good.

### 10. Consider `coverlet.collector` for code coverage

Neither test project includes a coverage collector package. If CI runs coverage, consider adding `coverlet.collector` centrally.

### 11. `NSubstitute` version is aligned (5.1.0 in both) — good, but should still be centralized

This is currently consistent, but without CPM, the next developer who updates it in one project may forget the other.

---

## 🟢 Positive — Things Done Well

- ✅ All projects are **modern SDK-style** — no legacy format to migrate
- ✅ `TreatWarningsAsErrors` is enabled everywhere — strong quality gate
- ✅ `EnforceCodeStyleInBuild` is enabled everywhere — consistent code style
- ✅ `Nullable` is enabled everywhere — good null-safety posture
- ✅ Test projects correctly set `IsPackable=false`
- ✅ `ProjectReference` paths are correct and well-structured (src → src, test → src)
- ✅ The project structure (src/test split) is clean and conventional

---

## 🛠️ Consolidated Fix — Recommended New Files

### **`/Directory.Build.props`** (new)

```xml
<Project>

  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
    <EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>true</EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>
    <Company>Contoso</Company>
    <Authors>Contoso Engineering</Authors>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <!-- Documentation XML for src projects only -->
  <PropertyGroup Condition="'$(IsTestProject)' != 'true'">
    <DocumentationFile>$(OutputPath)$(AssemblyName).xml</DocumentationFile>
  </PropertyGroup>

</Project>
```

> **Note on `DocumentationFile` condition:** The condition uses `$(IsTestProject)` which is set by `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk`. Since this is a `.props` file and `IsTestProject` is set during SDK import (which happens between `.props` and `.targets`), this condition will evaluate correctly. Alternatively, you could use a path-based convention: `Condition="!$(MSBuildProjectDirectory.Contains('test'))"`.

**🔴 Critical issues:**
1. **Package version mismatches** — `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions` differs (8.0.0 vs 8.0.1), test packages differ significantly (xunit 2.7→2.8, Test.Sdk 17.9→17.10)
2. **Redundant `System.Text.Json`** in the Web API project (already in shared framework)

**🟡 Anti-patterns:**
3. **6 properties copy-pasted** across all 5 projects (TFM, Nullable, Company, etc.)
4. **`DocumentationFile`** and **`PrintBuildInfo` target** duplicated in all 3 src projects
5. **No Central Package Management** — versions will keep drifting

**🟢 Recommended fix — create 3 new files:**
- **`Directory.Build.props`** — centralizes shared properties + DocumentationFile
- **`Directory.Build.targets`** — owns the PrintBuildInfo target (once)
- **`Directory.Packages.props`** — enables CPM, pins all versions in one place

This reduces total project file lines by ~58% and makes TFM upgrades a 1-line change.

Want me to apply these changes?
